scope: Proposition 9.4 (Suppression of essential polygons) of the manuscript “Cylinder loop weights and planar nesting” (preprints/Cylinder-loop-weights-and-planar-nesting-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e5effc6ded13360), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 77-78. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: On the balanced cylinder with period V = iN √ 3/2, let [ℓ] range over simple essential polygons modulo integer horizontal translations, and set W(ℓ) = ρ|ℓ|. If dx(ℓ) is their horizontal span, then ∑︂ [ℓ] W(ℓ) ≍ N−1 , ∑︂ [ℓ] W(ℓ)dx(ℓ) ≤ C. (77) 77 The total weight of essential polygons separating the two marked points in the balanced two-marker geometry is bounded uniformly in N. At each fixed nonnegative fugacity, deleting all these polygons changes its partition function by at most a bounded multiplicative factor.
